hero.headline: DeSantis signs death warrant for killer of Indian River County deputy
hero.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the death warrant Friday for William Reaves, the man convicted of killing Indian River County Deputy Richard Raczkoski in 1986. The execution is set for October 20, and Reaves has one last chance at an appeal.

Marc Raczkoski, the slain deputy's younger brother, said the warrant brings closure after 40 years. Marc Raczkoski was 22 when his 29-year-old brother was killed. He said the years without resolution took a toll on his entire family.

Deputy Richard Raczkoski answered a 911 call at a convenience store in Indian River County on December 23, 1986. Minutes later, he was shot four times and killed. Authorities arrested 37-year-old William Reaves days later in Albany, Georgia. Reaves was extradited to Indian River County, where he confessed to killing Raczkoski, saying he panicked when a gun fell out of his shorts and that he was under the influence of drugs at the time. Reaves was convicted of murder in 1987 and sentenced to death.

Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said the coming execution lifts weight from the agency. Flowers said he plans to attend the execution because he wants to make sure the last thing Reaves sees is an Indian River County deputy uniform. Marc Raczkoski recalled the middle-of-the-night knock on the door that changed everything. A friend on the Fort Pierce police department who knew his brother took him to the hospital, but Marc knew Richard had not survived.

The execution would mark Florida's 18th this year, following 19 executions in 2025. Grace Hanna of Floridians Against the Death Penalty raised concerns about how quickly executions are being carried out and the transparency of the process. Hanna said her own family member was murdered and understands everyone processes grief differently.

Marc Raczkoski described his brother as someone always focused on public service who was quick to make you laugh. Richard Raczkoski is buried at Hillcrest Memorial Gardens in Fort Pierce. Marc Raczkoski said the pain will always be there, but the execution gives him some closure for what Reaves did to his brother.
hero.article_text: At Hillcrest Memorial Gardens, Marc Raczkoski stares painfully at a place he's often tried to avoid. "Richard Raczkoski, beloved son, corporal, sheriff's department, Indian River County," reads Marc Raczkoski, blinking back tears. WATCH BELOW: Brother finally gets closure as Florida deputy killer's execution date setIt's the grave of his older brother, who was just 29 years old when he was buried at the Fort Pierce cemetery. "I was 22," Marc said quietly. "I was 22." It's always been an agonizing place for Marc — one that's brought up too many painful memories. Yet this time, his grief feels a little lighter. This time, for the first time in the 40 years he's come to visit his older brother, he finally has the answer he's been longing to give. And it's finally over," Marc said.Gov. Ron DeSantis on Friday signed the death warrant for William Reaves, the man convicted of killing Raczkoski in 1986. If carried out, the execution will mark Florida's 18th this year. 20, and Reaves has one last chance at an appeal."It gives closure," Marc said. "Now, when everybody asks me, 'What happened to the guy that murdered my brother?' That the first question I get, and I got to say, 'He's still — still hasn't happened." "You'll finally have a different answer," investigative reporter Kate Hussey supplied. "Yes, finally have a different answer," Marc replied. 23, 1986, 29-year-old Deputy Richard Raczkoski answered a 911 call at a convenience store in Indian River County. Minutes later, he was shot four times and killed, launching a multi-agency manhunt for the killer.Days later, authorities arrested 37-year-old William Reaves in Albany, Georgia, who was extradited to Indian River County, where he confessed to killing Raczkoski, saying he "panicked" when a gun fell out of his shorts, and that he was under the influence of drugs at the time. Forty years later, Marc said the memories of that night are still fresh and painful, recalling the middle-of-the-night knock on the door that changed everything. "One of the friends that was on the police department in Fort Pierce, my brother's friend, was at the back door. He took me up in the car and raced me up to the hospital, but I knew when they were talking to me in there for too long, I knew he didn't make it. I knew he didn't make it, and from then, it was just a blur of everything else after that," Marc told WPTV. "How could somebody do something like that? Richard was calling him a cab, for God's sake's. To empty his gun into him is beyond me. How could somebody do something like that?" In 1987, Reaves was convicted of murder and sentenced to death, yet for nearly four decades, Reaves sat on death row while Marc stood beside his brother's grave, waiting and wondering."Wondering what's happened. Feels like everybody forgot," Marc said.Marc said the years without resolution took a toll on his entire family."It's something I wouldn't wish on anybody to have to go through. And watch your parents go through," Marc said. "No more Christmas trees in the house. Holidays were never the same. Mom didn't decorate." When DeSantis signed Reaves' death warrant, Marc said the weight of the wait finally lifted."It's finally over. It's finally over," Marc said.The news also brought relief to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, and Sheriff Eric Flowers himself, who has pushed for Reaves' death warrant to be signed. "All of that is very heavy on our agency, and knowing that this execution is coming in October gives a little weight lifted off. I think it's going to be a moment of healing for our agency," Flowers told WPTV. Flowers said he plans to attend Reaves' execution. "Because I want to make sure the last thing he sees is an Indian River County Deputy uniform," said Flowers. Reaves' execution would mark Florida's 18th this year, following 19 executions in 2025, which set a modern-day record. The rapid pace has prompted concern from groups like Floridians Against the Death Penalty, who, along with capital defense attorneys, have raised concerns about how quickly executions are being carried out."One I think is around the transparency of this process. We don't know how people are being chosen for execution or why. We also don't know the impact this is having on corrections staff and those who are involved," Grace Hanna of Floridians Against the Death Penalty said.Hanna, though, knows the pain Raczkowski's family is experiencing. Her own family member was murdered, and said she understands everyone processes that grief differently. "And far be it for me to tell any family how they should feel. I can only speak to my own experience and my family's experience of having a loved one who was murdered, and I can say that I came out of that feeling that another death and another family's pain was not going to give us closure or peace," said Hanna. "Though certainly don't hold any ill will towards those who feel that this is what gives them closure." For Marc, standing at his brother's grave — a place that will always hold pain — he's reminded of all he's lost. "The time I never got to spend with him," Marc said, holding back tears. "Mom and Dad didn't see any closure in this, time that they didn't get to spend with him, time he didn't get to spend with my children, his nieces and nephews. It's all very much to take in." Marc described his brother as someone always focused on public service. "He was quick to make you laugh. He was always focused on public service, to serve people. He had found a man — an elderly man — that wandered away from a facility one time, and he's the one that found him out in the woods by the facility," Marc recalled. "He liked to fish and he liked the outdoors. And he was just basically fun to be around." Yet as he walks away from the grave, knowing the grief will never go away, he hopes the coming execution will bring something he has long sought."There is finally closure for Richard," Marc said. "For what he [Reaves] did to Richard, yes. What he did and the way he did it, yes, it gives me some closure, but still the pain will still always be there." hero.headline: Martin County High School sophomore arrested for hoax bomb threat
hero.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office arrested a 15-year-old Martin County High School student Tuesday in connection with a false bomb threat made against the school.

School resource officers and the criminal investigations division traced the originator of the message back to the male student, who is a sophomore at the school. The student confessed to sending the hoax threat and is facing a charge of false report concerning the planting of a bomb, a second-degree felony.

The arrest follows multiple hoax bomb threats involving schools in the area over the past several weeks. The sheriff's office said each threat is taken seriously and requires a significant response from law enforcement and emergency personnel, regardless of whether the threat ultimately proves to be a hoax. The suspect was only linked to the threat to the high school.

The sheriff's office warned that anonymous threats are traceable and will be prosecuted. Anyone who thinks sending a threat anonymously, by text, online or through another form of electronic communication will automatically protect them from being identified and charged is making an unsafe assumption, the sheriff's office said. The sheriff's office said it will thoroughly investigate these incidents and aggressively pursue those responsible when the investigation provides sufficient evidence to identify them.

hero.headline: National Democrats spend nearly $8M in Florida as seven races shift their way
hero.body:
The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee is spending nearly $8 million this week to defend Rep. Kathy Castor and other Florida incumbents after independent forecasters shifted seven Florida congressional races toward Democrats, raising fresh questions about whether the Republican mid-decade redistricting will produce its intended gains in November.

The national party spending includes ads in Castor's Tampa-area 14th District, putting resources behind an incumbent Republicans targeted with new boundaries drawn to create as many as four additional GOP seats. Democrats have called the redraw a potential dummymander, a partisan map that backfires on the party that designed it.

Inside Elections moved Castor's race to a toss-up on Sept. 17, following an earlier shift from lean Republican to tilt Republican. The forecaster rated the district solid Democratic before the redraw. Fox News and 22 Power Rankings shifted seven Florida congressional races toward Democrats, including Rep. Jared Moskowitz's 25th District race from toss-up to lean Democratic and Republican Rep. María Elvira Salazar's 27th District race from likely Republican to lean Republican. Fox attributed the changes largely to national polling favoring Democrats and movement toward the party among Hispanic voters.

Political consultant Michael Worley warned during the April redistricting debate that Republican advantages on paper might not translate into November victories. Worley, CEO of MDW Communications, pointed to uncertainty surrounding voters who had backed Republicans in previous elections. Gov. Ron DeSantis defended the redraw in August, calling it a good map while acknowledging a different political environment from 2022. This year they're winnable, but I think it's going to require some effort, DeSantis said of the four targeted seats.

The ratings changes do not establish that redistricting caused the movement, and seven shifts toward Democrats do not mean seven seats will change parties. Falling short of four Republican pickups would not, by itself, demonstrate that the map cost the GOP seats. Political scientist Susan MacManus said in a July 13 interview that Democrats would have to turn enthusiasm into votes. Turnout is a huge issue. That's how you win elections, MacManus said.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie MRI assault complaint details alleged statement by X-ray tech Gabriel Cruz
hero.body:
A traveling X-ray technician accused of sexually assaulting a patient at HCA Florida St. Lucie Hospital allegedly told her "Nobody can see what I can do to you" before bringing her into an MRI room, according to a Port St. Lucie police criminal complaint. Gabriel Cruz, 42, faces a first-degree felony charge of sexual battery involving a physically helpless or incapacitated victim.

The criminal complaint says officers responded to HCA Florida St. Lucie Hospital shortly after 8 a.m. on Sept. 14 after a patient reported that an X-ray technician had sexually assaulted her. The hospital's director of patient safety told officers the patient reported being sexually assaulted by a male Hispanic X-ray technician during the time of her MRI.

The patient told investigators Spanish is her primary language and that she had been admitted to the hospital after experiencing fainting spells and two falls that caused her to hit her head. She said she was transported from her room for an MRI at about 4 p.m. and that medication made her drowsy and she drifted in and out of sleep. She described the technician as a Hispanic man with a medium build who spoke Spanish and wore a blue shirt.

The patient told police that after the MRI she fell asleep. When she woke up, she alleged the technician had sexually assaulted her and was rubbing her hair. The report states he then cleaned her mouth with a white towel. Another person later transported the patient back to her room.

Hospital staff identified the technician as Gabriel Cruz, a traveling X-ray technician who had been under contract at the hospital since August. Police said surveillance video does not show inside the MRI room because there are no cameras there. However, the report states the video showed Cruz was the only person in the room with the patient during that time.

HCA Florida St. Lucie Hospital released a statement that said the facility contacted law enforcement and ended Cruz's assignment when the allegation was reported. "We do not tolerate behavior that jeopardizes the safety or security of our patients," the statement said. "We have assisted law enforcement throughout its investigation and remain focused on supporting our patient."

hero.headline: Martin County High School sophomore arrested on bomb-threat hoax charge
hero.body:
A 15-year-old Martin County High School student was arrested Tuesday and charged with making a false report concerning the planting of a bomb, a second-degree felony. Noah Taylor, a sophomore at the school, confessed to sending the threat during the investigation, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

The threat was quickly determined to be a hoax, and students and staff remained safe throughout the investigation, according to the school district. School resource officers and Criminal Investigations Division detectives traced the message back to Taylor, the Sheriff's Office said.

The arrest comes after multiple hoax bomb threats involving schools in the area in recent weeks. Investigators said they can only link Taylor to this specific threat. The threat was reported through FortifyFL, Principal Lori Vogel previously told families. The Sheriff's Office immediately began investigating and identified the apparent source of the message.

The district notified families Tuesday that an arrest had been made after initially telling parents an arrest appeared imminent. School officials said students found to have been involved in making threats could face both school disciplinary action and legal consequences. The district also reminded families that FortifyFL is an important tool for reporting legitimate safety concerns, but knowingly submitting false information or making a false threat can have serious consequences.

False threats are neither harmless nor funny, Vogel said, adding that they can cause fear, disrupt learning, and place a burden on students, families, school employees, and law enforcement. The Sheriff's Office said threats made anonymously, through text messages, online, or through other electronic communications, can still be traced and investigated.

hero.headline: Contract X-ray technician accused of sexually assaulting sedated patient at HCA St. Lucie Medical Hospital
hero.body:
A traveling X-ray technician has been accused of sexually assaulting a patient during an MRI procedure at HCA St. Lucie Medical Hospital, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Gabriel Cruz, 42, of Grant-Valkaria, was working as a contract technician at the hospital when the alleged assault occurred on Sept. 13. The hospital ended Cruz's assignment and contacted law enforcement when the allegation was reported.

The victim, a female patient who was receiving treatment for fainting episodes, reported the incident to hospital administration the following day. She had been brought to the emergency room by her nephew on Sept. 11 for evaluation after experiencing fainting spells and head injuries. She underwent a CT scan and was scheduled for an MRI two days later to further assess her condition.

The victim told investigators that Cruz made inappropriate comments before the procedure, allegedly telling her "nobody can see what I can do to you." During the MRI, the patient was given medication that made her drowsy. She reported waking up to find Cruz sexually assaulting her.

Hospital security footage from Sept. 13 shows Cruz entering the MRI room with the patient and later exiting while carrying an unknown object and wearing purple latex gloves. The video confirms Cruz was the only person in the MRI room with the victim during the time period in question. Cruz had been working at the hospital on contract since August 2026. The case has been forwarded to the Criminal Investigation Division for further investigation.

HCA St. Lucie Medical Hospital issued a statement on Sept. 17 saying, "We do not tolerate behavior that jeopardizes the safety or security of our patients. cards.headline: Port St. Lucie veterans home raises funds for WiFi, Medal of Honor Museum trip
cards.teaser: The Ardie R. Copas State Veterans Nursing Home in Port St. Lucie is raising money to provide WiFi access for residents and fund a trip to the Congressional Medal of Honor Museum in Sebring.
cards.body:
The Ardie R. Copas State Veterans Nursing Home in Port St. Lucie is raising money to provide WiFi access for residents and fund a trip to the Congressional Medal of Honor Museum in Sebring.

The fundraiser, organized with support from Ardies' Mission, includes a raffle for a Lincoln Town Car. Organizers said proceeds will help veteran residents stay connected with loved ones and experience a museum visit dedicated to honoring military service.

Shyrell Copas, daughter of Medal of Honor recipient Sgt. Ardie R. Copas, said her mother Betsy is the wife of Ardie Copas. Copas shared that when her father would go out into battle, he would grab his Betsy, his gun, and go to war.

The Ardie R. Copas State Veterans Nursing Home is a facility in the Tradition area of Port St. Lucie. Sherika Ayers, life enrichment program manager at the nursing home, said the facility has 120 beds and currently has a waiting list. The home is a five-star facility and nearly every room is occupied.

Veteran resident Cal Heathman shared artwork he created in recognition of America's 250th anniversary. Heathman said the research and the actual paintings took him about 10 months to do, starting last December thinking about what individual segments represented America.

The event highlighted the continued need for community support for veterans facilities and programs across the Treasure Coast, especially efforts focused on connection, recreation and quality of life for aging veterans. More information about the fundraiser and Ardies' Mission is available at ardiesmission.org.

hero.headline: Ex-boyfriend held gun to chin, threatened woman in Palm City SWAT standoff
hero.body:
A new arrest report reveals a man threatened to kill himself and his ex-girlfriend while armed and intoxicated before an hours-long SWAT standoff at a Palm City home. Darrel Abbey is now jailed without bond facing aggravated assault and battery charges.

According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office arrest report, Abbey's ex-girlfriend arrived at his home at about 12:08 p.m. after the two had broken up the previous night. She told investigators Abbey was not doing well mentally and had previously made comments about killing himself. When she arrived, Abbey had a rifle in his Tesla and a 10 mm handgun in his shorts, and appeared extremely intoxicated.

The arrest report says Abbey brought both firearms inside and began screaming at the woman while holding a gun. Abbey pointed the gun at her several times and threatened to kill her and her stepfather. At one point, Abbey placed the gun under his chin and pulled the trigger, but the firearm did not discharge because the magazine had been removed. The woman took the gun away from him as he began packing his vehicle, but Abbey continued reaching for it. When Abbey picked up the gun again, he said it was dangerous. Abbey continued drinking bourbon and Jameson throughout the encounter.

The woman told investigators she heard several loud pop sounds when Abbey walked outside. Abbey returned inside to retrieve a rifle and tried to get the woman to come outside and shoot it with him. Abbey told her he had hung a bucket from a nearby tree and was shooting at it. At some point during the incident, Abbey began cleaning the firearms and said he had to wipe all his fingerprints off and get the gunshot residue off his hands. Abbey said he was not going back to prison.

The report says Abbey later attempted to get into his vehicle while continuing to drink. When Abbey realized the woman was recording him, he reached for her phone. The woman ran down the road until a passing motorist stopped to help her.

Deputies later attempted to contact Abbey at the residence, but he refused to open the door or speak with them, leading to an hours-long standoff involving the Martin County Sheriff's Office SWAT team and hostage negotiators. Abbey was booked into the Martin County Jail without bond on charges including battery and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill. Investigators said Abbey is a convicted felon from Washington state with a prior conviction for vehicular assault.

hero.headline: Florida's left-lane law has drivers guessing on when it applies
hero.body:
Kevin Eddy drives from Stuart to Palm Beach County every day and said left-lane drivers are causing unwanted congestion on the roads. His frustration prompted a closer look at what Florida law actually requires and how well drivers understand the rule.

Florida law requires drivers to use the far-left lane mainly for passing and not as a general travel lane. The rule applies to roads with a speed limit of 65 mph or higher.

When asked whether they knew it was illegal to drive in the left lane, several drivers admitted confusion. Alfredo Milian said he did not know about the law. Another driver called it a gray area, while a third said he had heard it was illegal to drive in the left lane for a long period of time and that drivers should always use the right lane.

Eddy said better signage and stronger enforcement could help clarify the rule for drivers. He noted there are hardly any signs on the roads explaining the restriction. He also said Florida has many tourists who are not familiar with state traffic laws.

There are exceptions to the left-lane rule during heavy traffic congestion. Drivers should always merge back to the right after passing another car.

hero.headline: Contract X-ray technician accused of sexually assaulting sedated patient at HCA St. Lucie Hospital
hero.body:
A traveling X-ray technician has been accused of sexually assaulting a patient during an MRI procedure at HCA St. Lucie Medical Hospital, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

Gabriel Cruz, 42, of Grant-Valkaria, was working as a contract technician at the hospital when the alleged assault occurred on Sept. 13. The victim, a female patient who was receiving treatment for fainting episodes, reported the incident to hospital administration the following day.

The patient had been brought to the emergency room by her nephew on Sept. 11 for evaluation after experiencing fainting spells and head injuries. She underwent a CT scan and was scheduled for an MRI two days later to further assess her condition.

The victim told investigators that Cruz made inappropriate comments before the procedure, allegedly telling her "nobody can see what I can do to you." During the MRI, the patient was given medication that made her drowsy. She reported waking up to find Cruz sexually assaulting her.

Hospital security footage from Sept. 13 shows Cruz entering the MRI room with the patient and later exiting while carrying an unknown object and wearing purple latex gloves. The video confirms Cruz was the only person in the MRI room with the victim during the time period in question.

Cruz had been working at the hospital on contract since August 2026. The case has been forwarded to the Criminal Investigation Division for further investigation.

HCA St. Lucie Medical Hospital issued a statement on Sept. 17 saying the hospital does not tolerate behavior that jeopardizes the safety or security of patients. When the allegation was reported, the hospital contacted law enforcement and ended Cruz's assignment. The hospital said it has assisted law enforcement throughout the investigation and remains focused on supporting the patient.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce home with woman, 4 children struck by gunfire on Avenue L
hero.body:
Fort Pierce police are investigating a shooting that struck a home occupied by a woman and four children, with bullets penetrating a bedroom where a child was sleeping.

Officers responded to the 3100 block of Avenue L at 9:07 p.m. Friday, Sept. 18, after receiving reports of shooting activity. When they arrived, they discovered the home had been struck by multiple rounds of gunfire. Multiple rounds penetrated the residence, including the bedroom where a child was sleeping.

Officers located multiple bullet impacts on the exterior of the home. No injuries were reported.

hero.headline: Police chief details how road rage escalated to shooting on SW Brevity Terrace
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk released a detailed account of how a road rage confrontation near Southwest California Boulevard and Southwest Brevity Terrace escalated into a shooting Thursday evening, explaining the legal reasoning behind charging both drivers with felonies even though the shooter claimed self-defense.

The confrontation began as a misunderstanding during a lane change and merge near Southwest Crosstown Parkway. The situation turned violent when 41-year-old Dean Plotts exited his vehicle, approached 57-year-old Tylon Kukielka who was seated in his car, and punched him through the window.

"He stepped out of his vehicle, approached the other man who was seated inside his vehicle, and punched him inside his vehicle, so now he's breaking the plane of the window," Niemczyk said. "Therefore, entering, which makes it a burglary of the conveyance with the intention of committing a crime, being battery by punching the other individual who is seated inside the vehicle."

Plotts then returned to his vehicle, but the confrontation escalated further. "Almost makes it back to his vehicle and starts getting fire on," Niemczyk said. Kukielka fired a handgun, striking Plotts twice.

When asked if Kukielka's actions could be considered self-defense, Niemczyk explained why the shooting did not qualify. "It's not self-defense at that point. If Plotts had been coming at him at that point, the shooting may well have been justified, but it was actually just the reverse. He was fleeing from him," Niemczyk said.

Police received a 911 call around 6:30 p.m. reporting gunshots in the residential neighborhood. "Gunshots in front of my house," a caller said during the emergency call. The caller described the aftermath: "I heard it, and then I saw a guy raising his hands up and said he had blood on his hands."

Both men were arrested and now face felony charges. "Because one thought the other one may have cut the other one off when they were both turning into the same roadway. Again, no reason to be facing felony charges; let it go, let it go," Niemczyk said.

hero.headline: Indiantown data center plan returns with waterless design, but residents remain opposed
hero.body:
A proposal to build a 606-acre data processing center in Indiantown has returned with significant changes after being withdrawn in April, but many residents at an open house Monday said the revisions have not addressed their concerns about the project's impact on the community.

Developers Panatonni and Ferreira presented the revised plan for Project Silver Fox, which now includes a waterless design that would not use Indiantown's water resources. Adam Kramer, an executive with Project Silver Fox, said the new plan includes natural landscaping with retained trees to block views of the data center and a reduced facility size. The project would be built on land already zoned for industrial use at the former site of a power plant.

Kramer said the project represents a billion-dollar investment that would create jobs and tax revenue for the village. Kloee Ciuperger, the CEO of the Economic Council of Indiantown, said the tax revenue could fund youth athletics, parks, and water and wastewater infrastructure. Project officials said noise levels will remain within village code, there will be no ongoing vibrations, and local water pressure will not be affected.

Penny Kaminsky-Preli, an Indiantown resident, said the facility is too close to homes and a school. She said the school is within 2.2 miles of the proposed site and teachers would be subjected to sound and heat five days a week. Kaminsky-Preli called the project a money grab and land grab. Other residents at the open house voiced concerns about constant noise, heat from the facility, and impacts on farmland and families.

The Indiantown Village Council is expected to make a decision on the site plan in the coming months, according to Kramer. If approved, construction could begin in phases as early as 2027.

cards.headline: Sheriff confirms former Fox News producer Jennifer Eckhart died by suicide in Hobe Sound
cards.teaser: Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek publicly confirmed that former Fox Business producer Jennifer Eckhart died by suicide at her Hobe Sound home Saturday morning, addressing online conspiracy theories that suggested foul play.
cards.body:
Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek publicly confirmed Monday that former Fox Business producer Jennifer Eckhart died by suicide at her Hobe Sound home Saturday morning, directly addressing conspiracy theories that had suggested she was murdered.

Budensiek said he usually does not comment on suicides but decided to speak publicly about Eckhart's death to address the conspiracy theories. Investigators spent extensive time at the scene and investigated the death as if it was a homicide, he said. All evidence points to suicide, and the case remains open pending toxicology results.

Eckhart was a podcaster and former associate producer at Fox Business who gained notoriety after accusing a Fox News anchor of raping her. Investigators said she had family and friends who tried to help her, but she had been in and out of mental health facilities and had stopped taking her medications.

Elizabeth Burrows, director of development and communications with 211 Palm Beach and Treasure Coast, emphasized the tragedy of suicide and encouraged those struggling to seek help. Anyone in crisis can call 211 or 988, which are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, to provide resources or someone to talk to. Burrows said asking someone about suicide does not make it more of a risk. Asking about it lets that person know they are not alone, she said.

hero.headline: Police chief explains why shooter faces tougher charge than puncher in Port St. Lucie road rage case
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk publicly detailed how a lane-change misunderstanding escalated into a Thursday evening shooting on Southwest Brevity Terrace, and explained why 57-year-old Tylon Kukielka, who fired the shots, faces more serious charges than 41-year-old Dean Plotts, who threw the first punch.

Police received a 911 call around 6:30 p.m. reporting gunshots in a residential neighborhood near Southwest California Boulevard and Southwest Brevity Terrace. The altercation began as a misunderstanding during a lane change and merge near Southwest Crosstown Parkway. Plotts exited his vehicle, approached Kukielka, who was seated in his car, and punched him through the window.

"He stepped out of his vehicle, approached the other man who was seated inside his vehicle, and punched him inside his vehicle, so now he's breaking the plane of the window," Niemczyk said. "Therefore, entering, which makes it a burglary of the conveyance with the intention of committing a crime, being battery by punching the other individual who is seated inside the vehicle."

Plotts then returned to his vehicle, but Kukielka fired a handgun, striking Plotts twice. When asked if Kukielka's actions could be considered self-defense, Niemczyk said it was not. "If Plotts had been coming at him at that point, the shooting may well have been justified, but it was actually just the reverse. He was fleeing from him," Niemczyk said.

Both men were arrested and are facing felony charges. A 911 caller described the aftermath: "I heard it, and then I saw a guy raising his hands up and said he had blood on his hands."

Niemczyk urged residents to avoid escalating road rage disputes. "Because one thought the other one may have cut the other one off when they were both turning into the same roadway. Again, no reason to be facing felony charges; let it go, let it go," Niemczyk said.

Deputies were called to a residence on Southwest Bessey Creek Trail near Murphy Road Saturday following reports of shots fired outside the home, according to the sheriff's office. Road patrol deputies, detectives, SWAT and the Hostage Negotiation Team responded to the scene. The sheriff's office asked people to avoid the area until further notice. The sheriff's office has not provided a public update on how the situation was resolved or whether anyone was taken into custody.

hero.headline: Sheriff confirms former Fox News producer Jennifer Eckhart died by suicide in Hobe Sound
hero.body:
Former Fox News producer Jennifer Eckhart was found dead in her Hobe Sound home Saturday morning in what authorities have confirmed was a suicide, Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said during a news conference. A relative discovered Eckhart's body at her residence and contacted the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Budensiek described the scene as gruesome and horrific.

The sheriff said he typically does not comment on suicides but addressed rumors circulating about Eckhart's death, including speculation that she may have been murdered. Budensiek directly rebutted that speculation, explaining that the physical evidence made such theories impossible. He stated that based on the physical evidence in the house, it would be impossible for another human being to be in that space without leaving some type of fingerprint, shoeprint or some indication that another human was present.

Eckhart was perhaps most well known for accusing a Fox News anchor of raping her in 2020. The case was settled in 2024 before it went to trial. The circumstances surrounding her professional career at Fox News had kept her in the public eye in recent years.

Those experiencing a mental health crisis or who know someone in need of help can contact the Suicide Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988, or by accessing their online chat service. The 211 Helpline of Palm Beach and Treasure Coast is also available by dialing 211, or by texting a ZIP code to 898211. Mental health professionals are available through these services to provide support and resources to individuals in crisis.

hero.headline: Jolly refuses to debate Donalds, setting up Florida's first debate-free governor's race in 50 years
hero.body:
Democrat David Jolly said Sunday he will not debate Republican Byron Donalds before the Nov. 3 election, a decision that means Florida will hold its first governor's race without a televised debate in more than 50 years. The announcement triggered a new clash between the two major-party nominees, who accuse each other of avoiding voters.

Jolly announced his decision on MS NOW, telling Rev. Al Sharpton that Donalds acts in bad faith and continues to peddle lies. Donalds responded by pointing to Jolly's earlier willingness to debate him. The campaigns had accepted different debate invitations but never agreed to the same events. Jolly accepted proposed forums with CBS Miami's Jim DeFede and the Tampa Tiger Bay Club. Donalds announced he had accepted three other events involving Spectrum News and Florida A&M University, News4Jax, and Telemundo and NBC 6. Donalds' campaign said its proposed debates would feature two podiums and no audience. Jolly's campaign said it learned of those arrangements through a news release. Jolly said in a statement that Donalds refused the invitations Jolly had accepted and instead set his own rules by press release.

Jolly said Donalds is avoiding scrutiny of his property insurance proposal and other policies. Jolly's statement also linked to fact-checks of Donalds' campaign attacks. PolitiFact rated false a claim that Jolly wants higher taxes on tips, overtime and Social Security. Jolly is now citing reasoning Donalds used during the Republican primary, when Donalds declined calls to debate his primary opponents. At a Florida Chamber event, Donalds compared the campaign to applying for a job. Jolly said it is not his job to give Donalds a platform. He said his campaign has held more than 300 town halls and community meetings and will continue meeting voters and conducting online outreach.

Political analyst Dr. Susan MacManus said debates offer candidates free exposure and give voters, including those still undecided, a chance to compare the contenders directly. MacManus said declining interest in politics and lengthy televised events can reduce debates' appeal. Candidates may see more value in knocking on doors, holding town halls or doing local interviews. Artificial intelligence and social media add another consideration, she said. Misleading posts and manipulated material can spread while a debate is underway, potentially shaping perceptions before the candidates leave the stage. But refusing to participate can also alienate voters, MacManus said.

hero.headline: Indian River County's Operation Late Checkout nets over 50 arrests in human trafficking sting
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Thursday that law enforcement made more than 50 arrests during a four-day operation called Operation Late Checkout that targeted human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in the county. The operation ran from Sept. 13 and netted over 60 contacts, more than 50 arrests, and three ICE detainers.

Flowers announced the results alongside a representative from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. Agencies involved in the operation included the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Seminole County Sheriff's Office, Altamonte Springs Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecutor and the U.S. Attorney's Office.

During the operation, several victims were identified, and ongoing investigations are underway. Flowers said there are no specific arrests on human trafficking charges at this time. One case involved a man who traveled to Indian River County to meet a minor. The arrest was the result of the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force working across agencies to apprehend individuals attempting to lure children online.

Undercover teams were deployed in a variety of capacities during the operation. Victims' advocates trained to work with trafficking victims were on hand to speak with women involved in prostitution to determine whether they were being trafficked. Flowers called the operation unprecedented for Indian River County. FDLE Assistant Special Agent in Charge Alfonso Williams said Operation Late Checkout was initiated by FDLE in coordination with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office and is the first operation of this magnitude conducted in the county. Williams said the operation focused on identifying human trafficking victims, reducing the demand for prostitution, and apprehending individuals seeking sexual contact with minors. FDLE houses the Florida Trafficking Hotline at 1-855-352-7233.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie advances $2.2B mobility plan with $1.7B funding gap, phased fee hikes
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved Ordinance 26-89 on first reading Monday, advancing the city's 2050 Mobility Plan and an updated mobility-fee schedule that will increase development charges in phases between 2027 and 2030. The 25-year plan carries an estimated cost of approximately $2.2 billion, though approximately $1.7 billion of the plan is currently unfunded.

The updated fee schedule would increase charges paid by developers, contractors or owner-builders on new construction and certain property changes. The difference between current fees and newly calculated rates would be imposed in four steps: 25% of the increase in 2027, 50% in 2028, 75% in 2029 and the full rate in 2030. For a new 2,000-square-foot single-family home east of Interstate 95, the mobility fee would increase from approximately $3,200 today to $3,600 in 2027 and $4,800 by 2030. Developers could factor the added expense into the prices of new homes, rents or commercial projects. One council member raised concerns Monday about balancing infrastructure needs with the potential effect on housing affordability.

The short-term plan through 2030 carries an estimated cost of approximately $403 million and includes widening St. Lucie West Boulevard from four lanes to six between Interstate 95 and Cashmere Boulevard, widening Torino Parkway from two lanes to four between Midway Road and Cashmere Boulevard, and widening California Boulevard from two lanes to four between St. Lucie West Boulevard and Crosstown Parkway. Other proposed short-term projects include widening St. Lucie Boulevard from two lanes to four between Paar Drive and the Martin County line, continuing improvements along Floresta Drive between Prima Vista Boulevard and Crosstown Parkway, and widening Village Green Drive between Walton Road and Tiffany Avenue. The plan also calls for building or extending several roads to improve connections through growing areas of the city.

Port St. Lucie has used mobility fees since 2021. The program collected more than $30 million between 2022 and 2024. Unlike traditional road impact fees, the money can support sidewalks, shared-use paths, trails, bicycle lanes, transit stops, mobility hubs and intersection improvements. The city held public workshops on the plan and proposed fee schedule Sept. 2 and 3. The ordinance must return to City Council for final approval. If adopted, the ordinance and updated fee schedule would take effect in December.

cards.headline: Man charged after confrontation leads to shooting at Port St. Lucie Pollo Tropical
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police charged a 37-year-old man with attempted aggravated battery and felony battery after he confronted another man with two knives in a restaurant parking lot and was shot Saturday afternoon.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police charged a 37-year-old man with attempted aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and felony battery after he confronted another man with two knives in a restaurant parking lot and was shot Saturday afternoon.

Christopher Harris faces the charges following an incident at the Pollo Tropical located at 1365 NW St. Lucie West Boulevard, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. The shooting happened around 3:45 p.m. Saturday.

A 25-year-old man had entered the restaurant to pick up a food delivery order when Harris followed him inside, despite not appearing to place or pick up an order himself. When the man left the restaurant, Harris followed him outside. Outside surveillance footage showed Harris pushing the man and advancing toward him while the victim backed away. Witnesses reported seeing Harris with a knife just before the shooting.

The 25-year-old fired one round, striking Harris in the chest. Harris then went back inside the restaurant, where bystanders began providing aid and called 911. Officers responding to reports of gunfire found Harris suffering from a gunshot wound to the upper torso. He was airlifted to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

During the investigation, officers recovered a knife that had been removed from Harris' waistband while he was receiving medical attention. A second knife was later found in Harris' front pocket. The shooter was detained at the scene while detectives investigated and recovered the firearm.

Based on evidence, witness statements and surveillance footage, detectives determined Harris was the primary aggressor in the confrontation. Harris will be booked into the St. Lucie County Jail upon his medical release from the hospital. No criminal charges are pending against the shooter at this time.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie advances $2.2 billion 2050 Mobility Plan with phased fee hikes
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved Ordinance 26-89 on first reading Monday, advancing the city's 2050 Mobility Plan with an updated mobility fee schedule that would increase charges on new development in phases beginning in 2027. The 25-year roadmap carries an estimated cost of approximately $2.2 billion, with $1.7 billion currently unfunded.

The plan identifies transportation infrastructure needed to support continued growth in Port St. Lucie, which has reached more than 260,000 residents across approximately 120 square miles. Projects include new and wider roads, intersection improvements, sidewalks, trails, bicycle facilities and transit. A presenter told council during Monday's meeting that not enough money exists to fund every single project in the mobility plan.

Under the updated fee schedule, developers, contractors and owner-builders would pay higher one-time mobility fees tied to new development, redevelopment, additions and certain changes in property use. The difference between current rates and newly calculated rates would be imposed in four steps: 25 percent of the increase in 2027, 50 percent in 2028, 75 percent in 2029 and the full rate in 2030. For a new 2,000-square-foot home east of Interstate 95, the fee would rise from approximately $3,200 today to $3,600 in 2027 and $4,800 by 2030. One council member raised concerns about the potential effect higher development costs could have on housing affordability.

The short-term plan through 2030 carries an estimated cost of approximately $403 million. Proposed projects include widening St. Lucie West Boulevard from four lanes to six between Interstate 95 and Cashmere Boulevard, widening Torino Parkway from two lanes to four between Midway Road and Cashmere Boulevard, and widening California Boulevard from two lanes to four between St. Lucie West Boulevard and Crosstown Parkway. The plan also proposes widening St. Lucie Boulevard from two lanes to four between Paar Drive and the Martin County line and continuing improvements along Floresta Drive between Prima Vista Boulevard and Crosstown Parkway.

Port St. Lucie has used mobility fees since 2021. The program collected more than $30 million between 2022 and 2024. Unlike traditional road impact fees, the money can support sidewalks, shared-use paths, trails, bicycle lanes, transit stops, mobility hubs and intersection improvements. The city held public workshops on the plan and fee schedule Sept. 2 and 3. The ordinance must return to City Council for final approval. If adopted, the ordinance and updated fee schedule would take effect in December.

hero.headline: Christopher Harris charged as primary aggressor after shooting at Port St. Lucie Pollo Tropical
hero.body:
Police determined Christopher Harris was the primary aggressor in a Port St. Lucie Pollo Tropical parking lot confrontation that ended with Harris shot in the upper torso and charged with attempted aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and felony battery based on a prior battery conviction.

Officers with the Port St. Lucie Police Department responded to the Pollo Tropical at 1635 NW St. Lucie West Blvd. on September 19 and found Harris suffering from gunshot wounds to his upper torso. The other person involved, identified as Isaiah Davis, 25, was detained at the scene while officers investigated. Police also recovered and secured a firearm.

Interviews and surveillance video from the restaurant showed the confrontation between Harris and Davis began after the two men had an interaction in the parking lot. Davis entered the restaurant to pick up a delivery order, and Harris followed him inside despite not appearing to place or pick up an order. When Davis left the restaurant, Harris followed him outside. Surveillance video showed Harris, who was armed with a knife, push Davis and then advance toward him as Davis backed away. Davis then pulled out a gun and fired one round, striking Harris in the upper torso.

Harris returned to the restaurant, where people began rendering aid and called 911. During the investigation, officers recovered one knife from Harris' waistband while aid was being provided and another from his front pocket. Harris was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment. Based on surveillance video, witness statements and other evidence, detectives determined Harris was the primary aggressor. Police said Harris will be booked into the St. Lucie County Jail once he is medically released from the hospital.

hero.headline: Man arrested after SWAT standoff, shots fired at Palm City home
hero.body:
A 38-year-old man is in custody after a SWAT standoff Sunday at a Palm City home following reports of shots fired and a domestic-related aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. Darrel Levon Abbey was arrested in connection with the incident on Southwest Bessey Creek Trail, near Murphy Road.

Abbey faces three charges: felony aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill, misdemeanor battery touch or strike, and misdemeanor use of a firearm under the influence of alcohol. The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the situation has been safely resolved.

Deputies initially responded to reports of shots fired outside the residence. Additional calls indicated the incident was domestic-related and involved an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.

Abbey barricaded inside the home. SWAT and the Hostage Negotiation Team worked to safely resolve the situation.

hero.headline: Christopher Harris charged as aggressor in Port St. Lucie Pollo Tropical shooting
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police have filed charges against Christopher Harris, 37, after determining he was the primary aggressor in a September 19 confrontation outside a Pollo Tropical restaurant that ended with him being shot. Harris faces attempted aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and felony battery charges, while the shooter faces no criminal charges.

Officers responded around 3:43 p.m. September 19 to the restaurant at 1365 NW St. Lucie West Boulevard and found Harris suffering from a gunshot wound to his upper torso. He was flown to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Isaiah Davis, 25, was detained at the scene while detectives investigated. Officers recovered a firearm.

Surveillance video showed Harris following Davis inside the restaurant despite not appearing to place or pick up an order, police said. Davis had entered to pick up a food delivery order. Exterior surveillance showed Harris pushing Davis and advancing toward him as Davis moved backward. Investigators said Harris was armed with a knife during the confrontation, and witnesses reported seeing him with a knife shortly before the shooting. Davis fired one round, striking Harris in the chest.

Harris went back inside the restaurant, where people provided aid and called 911. One knife was recovered after it had been removed from Harris's waistband while people were helping him, police said. Another knife was later found in his front pocket. After reviewing surveillance video, physical evidence and witness statements, detectives determined Harris was the primary aggressor and established probable cause for the charges. The felony battery charge is based on a prior battery conviction. Police said an arrest affidavit was submitted to the St. Lucie County jail. Harris is expected to be booked after he is medically released from the hospital.

hero.headline: Palm City SWAT standoff followed threats, gunfire and attempts to destroy evidence
hero.body:
A new arrest report reveals that Darrel Abbey threatened to kill himself and his ex-girlfriend, fired shots outside his Palm City home, and attempted to wipe away evidence before an hours-long SWAT standoff with the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

According to the arrest report, Abbey's ex-girlfriend arrived at his home at about 12:08 p.m. after the two had broken up the previous night. She told investigators Abbey was not doing well mentally and had previously made comments about killing himself. When she arrived, Abbey had a rifle in his Tesla and a 10 mm handgun in his shorts and appeared to be extremely intoxicated.

The report says Abbey brought both firearms inside the home and began screaming at the woman while holding a gun. Investigators said Abbey pointed the gun at her several times and threatened to kill her and her stepfather. At one point, Abbey allegedly placed the gun under his chin and pulled the trigger, but the firearm did not discharge because the magazine had been removed. When Abbey picked up the gun again after the woman had taken it from him, he said, "This is really f***** dangerous now," according to the report.

Investigators said Abbey continued drinking bourbon and Jameson throughout the encounter. The woman told investigators she heard several loud sounds as Abbey walked outside. Abbey then returned inside to retrieve a rifle and allegedly tried to get the woman to come outside and shoot it with him. When she asked what he was shooting at, Abbey allegedly told her he had hung a bucket from a nearby tree and was shooting at it.

At some point during the incident, Abbey allegedly began cleaning the firearms and said, "I gotta wipe all my fingerprints off, I gotta get the gunshot residue off of my hands, I'm not going back to prison," according to the report. The report says Abbey later attempted to get into his vehicle while continuing to drink, prompting the woman to begin recording him. Investigators who reviewed the video said Abbey appeared intoxicated while sitting in the driver's seat, slurred his words and struggled to hold his head upright.

When Abbey realized the woman was recording, he allegedly reached for her phone. The woman then ran down the road until a passing motorist stopped to help her. Deputies later attempted to contact Abbey at the residence, but he refused to open the door or speak with them, leading to an hours-long standoff involving the Martin County Sheriff's Office SWAT team and hostage negotiators.

Abbey was booked into the Martin County Jail without bond on charges including battery and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill. Investigators also said Abbey is a convicted felon from Washington state with a prior conviction for vehicular assault.

Investigators said Abbey later began packing his vehicle. Fearing he was going to shoot her stepfather, the woman took the gun away from him, but Abbey allegedly continued reaching for it as she begged him to stop. The report says that when Abbey picked up the gun again, he said, "This is really f***** dangerous now." Investigators said Abbey continued drinking bourbon and Jameson throughout the encounter. As Abbey walked outside, the woman told investigators she heard several loud "pop" sounds. Abbey then returned inside to retrieve a rifle and allegedly tried to get the woman to come outside and shoot it with him. See also: Causeway Cove project fight escalates: Can Fort Pierce push back against state law? When she asked what he was shooting at, Abbey allegedly told her he had hung a bucket from a nearby tree and was shooting at it. At some point during the incident, Abbey allegedly began cleaning the firearms and said, "I gotta wipe all my fingerprints off, I gotta get the gunshot residue off of my hands, I'm not going back to prison." The report says Abbey later attempted to get into his vehicle while continuing to drink, prompting the woman to begin recording him. Investigators who reviewed the video said Abbey appeared intoxicated while sitting in the driver's seat, slurred his words and struggled to hold his head upright. When Abbey realized the woman was recording, he allegedly reached for her phone. The woman then ran down the road until a passing motorist stopped to help her. Deputies later attempted to contact Abbey at the residence, but he refused to open the door or speak with them, leading to an hours-long standoff involving the Martin County Sheriff's Office SWAT team and hostage negotiators. Abbey was booked into the Martin County Jail without bond on charges including battery and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill. Investigators also said Abbey is a convicted felon from Washington state with a prior conviction for vehicular assault.

cards.headline: 11-year-old describes hearing gunshots as SWAT surrounded Palm City street during standoff
cards.teaser: An 11-year-old Palm City boy recounted hearing several gunshots from his neighbor's yard Saturday before deputies evacuated his family during an hours-long SWAT standoff.
cards.body:
An 11-year-old Palm City boy recounted hearing several gunshots from his neighbor's yard Saturday before deputies evacuated his family during an hours-long SWAT standoff on SW Bessey Creek Trail near Murphy Road. Gavin Ryan, who lives next door to where the standoff occurred, said the incident frightened him because such events do not typically happen in his neighborhood. His mother said deputies asked her to evacuate after she heard several gunshots coming from her neighbor's yard, and SWAT officers later positioned themselves near her home as the standoff unfolded.

Martin County deputies responded to a domestic-related incident at the property Saturday and 38-year-old Darrel Abbey barricaded himself inside a guest house on the property. Deputies said Abbey was armed and dangerous and under the influence of alcohol. SWAT officers and hostage negotiators spent hours trying to convince him to surrender.

Another neighbor, Julian Tracy, said he was shocked to learn what was happening. Tracy said he had never heard about a shooting in someone's neighborhood before a neighbor told him about the incident.

Hostage negotiators worked throughout the afternoon to get Abbey to come out peacefully. He eventually surrendered without incident and no injuries were reported. Abbey was booked into the Martin County Jail and faces three charges, including felony aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. Jail records show he is being held on a $12,500 bond.

The fire occurred around 11:20 a.m. on the southbound side of the interstate. Martin County Fire Rescue responded to the scene to extinguish the blaze.

The driver was the only person on the bus at the time of the fire and was able to escape the vehicle. No injuries were reported in the incident.

One southbound lane of I-95 has since reopened to traffic. Authorities continue to investigate what caused the charter bus to catch fire.

cards.headline: Molly's House in Stuart marks 30 years of housing families during medical treatment
cards.teaser: The nonprofit organization in Stuart's medical district has provided affordable lodging and support services to patients and families receiving treatment on the Treasure Coast for three decades.
cards.body:
Molly's House in Stuart is celebrating 30 years of providing affordable lodging and support services for patients and families receiving medical treatment on the Treasure Coast. The nonprofit organization in Stuart's medical district was founded to help families stay close to doctors, hospitals and treatment providers during difficult medical situations.

Leaders with Molly's House said the mission continues to focus on reducing stress for families facing long-term care and recovery. The organization provides affordable lodging for guests traveling for treatment and also offers a free cancer support program for residents. Demand for support services remains strong as more families seek affordable options near treatment centers across South Florida and the Treasure Coast.

Kate Wiegerink, a member of the Molly's House board of directors and Molly Sharkey's sister, said the organization also works to educate new doctors, nurses and community members about the services available to patients and families. The nonprofit is celebrating the milestone with an open house Monday at its facility on Osceola Street in Stuart. Community members are invited to tour the house and healing garden while learning more about the organization's history and programs.

In addition to housing support, Molly's House provides weekly free meals to residents to help ease food expenses and preparation during stressful medical situations. Businesses and individuals can become a "Chef for a Day" and provide an average of 28 meals. Brandi Patricio, whose son TJ received treatment, shared how the nonprofit has helped her family manage the financial and emotional challenges tied to ongoing medical care. Patricio said having access to affordable lodging reduces anxiety about housing costs during treatment and allows families to focus on recovery and care.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie man charged after knife confrontation at Pollo Tropical ends with him being shot
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police have charged a 37-year-old man after surveillance footage and witness statements showed he was the aggressor in a knife confrontation that ended with him being shot outside a restaurant Saturday afternoon. No charges are pending against the 25-year-old shooter.

Christopher Harris faces attempted aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and felony battery charges following the incident at the Pollo Tropical located at 1365 NW St. Lucie West Boulevard, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. The shooting happened around 3:45 p.m. Saturday.

Police said Harris followed the 25-year-old man into the restaurant despite not appearing to place or pick up an order himself while the victim was picking up a food delivery order. When the victim left, Harris followed him outside. Surveillance footage showed Harris pushing the man and advancing toward him while the victim backed away. Witnesses reported seeing Harris with a knife just before the shooting.

The 25-year-old fired one round, striking Harris in the chest. Harris went back inside the restaurant, where bystanders provided aid and called 911. Officers found Harris suffering from a gunshot wound to the upper torso and he was airlifted to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

During the investigation, officers recovered a knife that had been removed from Harris' waistband while he was receiving medical attention. A second knife was later found in Harris' front pocket. The shooter was detained at the scene while detectives investigated and recovered the firearm.

Based on evidence, witness statements and surveillance footage, detectives determined Harris was the primary aggressor in the confrontation. He will be booked into the St. Lucie County Jail upon his medical release from the hospital.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman launches Chris's Place, free grief support community
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie woman who lost her husband in 2018 is building a new in-person grief support community on the Treasure Coast to fill what she saw as a gap in local resources.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman is launching Chris's Place, a free in-person grief support community on the Treasure Coast designed to help people navigating loss.

Stacey Comer created the community after her husband Chris died in 2018 following complications from a kidney transplant. As she learned to navigate life without him, Comer began to notice there wasn't one central place on the Treasure Coast where people experiencing grief could go to find support, resources and connection. She started asking herself a simple question: "Why isn't there an entity where all of this lives under?" That question became the foundation for Chris's Place.

Comer said grief can be difficult to understand until you experience it yourself. While friends and family often want to help, people who are grieving can still feel isolated. "You only sort of know it if you're in the club, and when you're in the club everyone wants to be so supportive and helpful," Comer said. Chris's Place is intended to give people a place to connect with others who understand what they're going through.

The community is not limited to people who have lost a spouse or immediate family member. Comer wants it to be available to anyone who has experienced a loss and needs support navigating what comes next. Right now, Comer is creating Chris's Place from the ground up. Her long-term vision is to create a physical space on the Treasure Coast where people can gather, find resources and connect with others who understand grief. "You are not alone. You feel alone because you think you're the only one feeling it, but you're not," Comer said. She wants other people on the Treasure Coast to have the kind of support she realized was missing during her own journey through grief.

hero.headline: Palm City man charged with felony domestic assault after SWAT standoff
hero.body:
A Palm City man is facing three charges, including a felony, after the Martin County Sheriff's Office SWAT Team resolved an armed barricade standoff at a home on Southwest Bessey Creek Trail. Devin Abbey, 38, was booked at the Martin County Jail with total bond set at $12,500.

Abbey faces aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill (domestic), a third-degree felony; battery, touch or strike (domestic), a first-degree misdemeanor; and use of a firearm under the influence of alcohol, a second-degree misdemeanor.

Deputies were called to a residence on Southwest Bessey Creek Trail near Murphy Road Saturday following reports of shots fired outside the home, according to the sheriff's office. Additional calls indicated the incident was domestic-related and involved an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, authorities said.

Around 4:30 p.m. Saturday, the sheriff's office described Abbey as armed and dangerous and said he was contained inside the residence. Road patrol deputies, detectives, SWAT and the Hostage Negotiation Team responded to the scene. The sheriff's office asked people to avoid the area until further notice. The sheriff's office has not provided a public update on how the situation was resolved.

hero.headline: Air Force confirms missing Eglin AFB attack drone recovered by Pensacola fishing charter
hero.body:
The Air Force confirmed that a drone went missing from testing at Eglin Air Force Base and was recovered by a fishing charter off the Florida Panhandle on Saturday. The drone appeared to be an FLM 136, a clone of the Iranian-designed Shahed-136 attack drone that has played a key role in current combat operations.

Hot Spots Charters, a fishing charter company out of Pensacola, discovered the drone floating offshore near Eglin Air Force Base, home of the Air Force's 96th Test Wing. Charter captain Daniel Arsenault wrote on Facebook that the crew made the surprising catch during a six-hour trip Saturday.

An Eglin Air Force Base spokesperson told defense news site The War Zone that the base was conducting a test when the test article went down. The spokesperson would not specify the type of drone. Photos shared by Hot Spots Charters showed the drone missing its nose section and rear propeller, taking up the entire bow section of the fishing boat.

The drone appeared to be part of the Air Force's Low-cost Unmanned Combat Attack System, or LUCAS, program announced late last year. The LUCAS drones are clones of the Iranian-designed Shahed-136 model. Manufactured by Arizona-based Spektreworks, the drones are 9.8 feet long, have a wingspan of 8.2 feet, and weigh 70 pounds. US Central Command announced in early March that LUCAS drones were being used in the war with Iran. Arsenault told CNN he came across the drone by chance while riding along offshore and saw it floating. The charter company later posted on Facebook that the drone had been retrieved, writing that black SUVs came and got their drone.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce commissioners vote to explore hiring outside counsel to challenge Causeway Cove development
hero.body:
Fort Pierce city commissioners approved a motion to explore hiring an outside land-use attorney to determine whether the city has any legal grounds to challenge the proposed Causeway Cove development under Florida's Live Local Act. The vote escalates a fight over the 913-unit waterfront project on South Hutchinson Island as construction could begin before the end of the year.

The proposed redevelopment would transform the Causeway Cove property along Seaway Drive with five towers ranging from 11 to 17 stories, 913 residential units, two hotels totaling 407 rooms, more than 72,000 square feet of retail and commercial space, and 218 marina slips, according to city records. The city is also monitoring lawsuits filed elsewhere in Florida that seek to restore greater local control over development decisions.

City officials have repeatedly said the proposed Causeway Cove project qualifies under the Live Local Act and therefore moves through an administrative review process rather than a traditional public hearing and commission vote. The law allows qualifying projects to bypass certain local zoning, density and height restrictions if affordability requirements are met. Qualifying developments must reserve at least 40% of units as affordable rental housing for at least 30 years.

Commissioner Michael Broderick said residents' concerns extend beyond the size of the development. "The concern is density, traffic flow," Broderick said, pointing to longstanding concerns about capacity on Seaway Drive. Resident Edie Harrison said the project would alter an area known for its waterfront views, boating access and small-town character. "Everything is still very quaint," Harrison said. "It's one of those gems."

Another major debate centers on affordability. Under Live Local, affordable housing calculations are based on regional income levels rather than income levels specific to Fort Pierce. According to city officials, some qualifying units could rent for more than $2,300 per month, while Fort Pierce's median rent is substantially lower. Broderick said many residents question whether those figures reflect true affordability within the city.

Land-use attorney Keith Poliakoff, who has represented clients in Live Local disputes across the state, said local governments generally have limited discretion once a project satisfies state requirements. Poliakoff said the law effectively requires municipalities to administratively approve qualifying projects, even when residents or local leaders oppose the density, height or scale of a development. State data show more than 200 Live Local projects have been proposed or approved across Florida. The most recent changes to the law, known as Live Local 4.0, took effect July 1, 2026, expanding eligible development sites and further clarifying protections for qualifying projects that include affordable housing.

hero.headline: Palm City SWAT standoff ends with arrest after man barricades in guest house
hero.body:
A 38-year-old man is facing felony charges after barricading himself inside a guest house on SW Bessey Creek Trail near Murphy Road in Palm City during an hours-long standoff with law enforcement Saturday. Darrel Abbey surrendered to SWAT officers and hostage negotiators after firing shots and prompting neighbor evacuations. He is being held on a $12,500 bond.

Deputies were initially called to the home for a domestic-related incident. The situation escalated when Abbey, who was armed and under the influence of alcohol, barricaded himself inside a guest house on the property, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

Neighbors were evacuated after gunshots were heard. The mother of 11-year-old Gavin Ryan, who lives next door, said deputies asked her to evacuate after she heard several gunshots coming from her neighbor's yard. SWAT officers positioned themselves near her home as the standoff unfolded. Hostage negotiators worked throughout the afternoon to get Abbey to come out peacefully. He eventually surrendered without incident and no injuries were reported.

Julian Tracy, another neighbor, said he was shocked to learn what was happening. Gavin Ryan said he was scared because it does not usually happen in the neighborhood.

Abbey was booked into the Martin County Jail and is facing three charges, including felony aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. Jail records show he is being held on a $12,500 bond.

"I was pretty scared because it doesn't usually happen in our neighborhood," said 11-year-old Gavin Ryan, who lives next door. He eventually surrendered without incident and no injuries were reported. Another neighbor, Julian Tracy, said he was shocked to learn what was happening. "[Gavin's] mom told me about it, and I was like, 'Whoa,' Tracy said. "I've never heard about a shooting in someone's neighborhood." Abbey was booked into the Martin County Jail and is facing three charges, including felony aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. Jail records show he is being held on a $12,500 bond.

hero.headline: SWAT standoff in Palm City ends with arrest after shots fired on Bessey Creek Trail
hero.body:
A Martin County SWAT standoff at a Palm City home ended peacefully with the arrest of a man on domestic aggravated assault and firearm charges after shots were fired at a residence on Southwest Bessey Creek Trail near Murphy Road.

Darrel Levon Abbey, 38, was arrested following the incident. He faces three charges: felony aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill, misdemeanor battery touch or strike, and misdemeanor use of a firearm under the influence of alcohol.

Deputies initially responded to reports of shots fired outside the residence. Additional calls indicated the incident was domestic-related and involved an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. Abbey barricaded inside the home before SWAT and the Hostage Negotiation Team worked to safely resolve the situation. The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the situation has been safely resolved.

hero.headline: Police investigate incident at Pollo Tropical in Port St. Lucie near I-95, Florida's Turnpike
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department is actively investigating an incident at Pollo Tropical on Northwest St. Lucie Boulevard. The restaurant is situated between Interstate 95 and Florida's Turnpike in Port St. Lucie.

Authorities have stated that the incident appears to be isolated, and there is no known threat to the public at this time. The investigation remains ongoing as police work to gather information about what occurred at the location.

Police are advising motorists to expect delays in the area surrounding the restaurant while the investigation continues. Drivers are being asked to use alternate routes if possible to avoid the affected area.

No additional details about the nature of the incident have been released at this time. The Port St. Lucie Police Department continues to investigate the situation.
